about-title: Public information should be easier to use
about-lede: BetterMati.org makes public information about the City of Mati, Davao Oriental easier to find, understand and verify.
about-note: A volunteer-run civic portal that organizes city services, government information, public funds and official-source data in one place.
about-flow-label: How BetterMati turns official sources into clearer public information
about-flow-origin-detail: Charters · Reports · Census data · Public records
about-flow-result-detail: Searchable · Structured · Linked to its source
about-why-title: Public information shouldn’t be hard to find just because it lives in different places
about-why-p1: Information about a city is spread across many places: charters and department pages, financial reports, census tables, council records, social media posts and PDF files. To find one answer, residents often need to know which office publishes it first.
about-why-p2: BetterMati brings those sources into one resident-facing structure while keeping the original source visible, so residents, students, researchers and civil society can find what they need without first learning how the City Government is organized.
about-why-goal: The goal is not to replace official sources. It is to make them easier to find, understand and check.
about-sources-title: Public information lives across many sources
about-dir-lede: Published public information, structured into six directories:
about-dir-services: Service guidance by category, with responsible offices and the sources behind each guide.
about-dir-government: Elected officials, City offices, barangays and official contact channels.
about-dir-legislation: How ordinances and resolutions move through the Sangguniang Panlungsod, with published records.
about-dir-transparency: City receipts and spending from DBM fiscal records.
about-dir-statistics: Population, barangays, income class and poverty estimates with their sources.
about-dir-visit: Places to see in Mati, the seasons and how to plan a trip.
about-today-note: Each collection has its own unit, coverage and reference period, so these figures shouldn’t be added together. They describe what BetterMati currently publishes, not every City dataset or record. If something isn’t on BetterMati, that doesn’t mean the record, office, service or document doesn’t exist.
about-process-title: From official source to usable civic information
about-process-lede: How information moves from a public source to a BetterMati page:
about-step-find-desc: An official public page, document, dataset or other attributable source.
about-step-check-desc: Who published it, when, and what it actually supports.
about-step-structure-desc: Organize the facts for residents without changing what the source says.
about-step-publish-desc: Show the source, its scope, the date it was checked and its limits.
about-principle-source-desc: Published facts stay connected to the public source they came from.
about-principle-scope-desc: A dataset is presented as what it covers, not as something broader.
about-principle-unknown-desc: Missing or unconfirmed information is marked, not guessed. That’s why many fees and contacts say “Confirm with office”.
about-principle-residents-desc: Information is organized around what people are trying to find or do.
about-we-do-organize: Organize public information from official sources
about-we-do-links: Keep source links and checked dates visible
about-we-do-independent: Run an independent, volunteer-built civic portal
about-we-dont-replace: Replace the official City Government website
about-we-dont-speak: Speak on behalf of the City Government
about-we-dont-alter: Create or change official government records
about-we-dont-infer: Fill in facts a source doesn’t support
about-we-dont-transact: Process applications, payments, complaints or emergency requests
about-trust-title: Built to be checked, not taken on authority
about-evidence-body: Wherever the public record allows, BetterMati keeps the path from a published fact back to its original source visible.
about-evidence-funds: City receipts and spending, with the DBM record behind them.
about-evidence-stats: Population and poverty figures, with their PSA sources.
about-evidence-services: Every service page lists the sources behind its guidance.
about-independent-official: Not an official City Government website
about-independent-official-desc: BetterMati.org is a volunteer-run initiative. It is not run by the City Government of Mati and does not replace official government channels.
about-independent-attribution: Source links are attribution, not endorsement
about-independent-attribution-desc: A link to an official source shows where information came from. It does not mean the government endorses or authored BetterMati.
about-independent-original: Use original sources for important decisions
about-independent-original-desc: For legal, administrative or financial decisions, check the linked original source or ask the responsible office.
about-open-title: Open, volunteer-built and free to use
about-open-body: BetterMati.org costs the people of Mati nothing. Its code is public on GitHub, and designers, developers, writers and translators are all welcome to help.

about-logo-link: The BetterMati logo: files and how to use them
logo-lede: What the logo shows, which version to use where, and the files to download.
logo-note: The files are free to use under CC BY 4.0, with credit to BetterMati.org.
logo-mark-title: The Sleeping Dinosaur, the sun and Pujada Bay
logo-mark-lede: The logo draws a view most people in Mati know: the Sleeping Dinosaur headland across Pujada Bay, with the sun behind it and the bay below.
logo-mark-figure: The BetterMati logo, with its four parts numbered: the Sleeping Dinosaur, the sun, Pujada Bay and the name.
logo-part-dinosaur-desc: The headland across Pujada Bay whose outline looks like a dinosaur lying down: a small head, a dip for the neck, then a long back. Drawn in Pujada navy.
logo-part-bay-desc: Two lines of waves in royal blue.
logo-part-name-desc: “Better Mati” in Pujada navy, with “.org” in the sun’s amber. The letters are drawn as shapes, so the logo looks the same everywhere without needing a font.
logo-versions-lede: Choose the version that suits the background. SVG stays sharp at any size; use PNG where SVG isn’t accepted.
logo-version-full-desc: The default. Use it on white or light backgrounds.
logo-version-white-desc: For navy, dark or photo backgrounds. The sun and “.org” stay amber.
logo-version-mark-desc: For when the name is already nearby, or the space is too small for the full logo.
logo-version-mark-white-desc: The mark for navy, dark or photo backgrounds.
logo-version-icon-desc: The round badge is the icon in browser tabs. The square version is for phone home screens, which crop it to their own shape.
logo-colors-lede: Use these exact values when you need to match the logo. Navy, royal blue and amber are also the site’s main colors.
logo-color-navy-use: The Sleeping Dinosaur and the name.
logo-color-sky-use: The sky inside the app icon.
logo-color-wave-use: The waves on the white logo and white mark.
logo-space-title: Give it room and keep it readable
logo-space-lede: The logo works best with space around it, and at a size where “.org” can still be read.
logo-space-clear-desc: Leave empty space around the logo at least as wide as the sun (x). Keep text, other logos and the edge of the page or photo outside it.
logo-space-figure: The full logo inside a dashed box. The gap on every side is as wide as the sun in the logo.
logo-space-min-full: Full logo: at least 100 px wide on screen, or 25 mm in print.
logo-space-min-mark: Mark only: at least 24 px wide on screen, or 8 mm in print. Smaller than that, use the app icon, which is made for browser tabs.
logo-usage-lede: The logo should always look like itself. These are the common ways it goes wrong.
logo-do-files: Use the files on this page as they are.
logo-do-background: Use the full-color logo on light backgrounds and the white logo on dark ones.
logo-do-space: Keep the clear space, and stay above the minimum size.
logo-do-credit: Credit BetterMati.org when you use it.
logo-dont-background: Put the full-color logo on a dark or busy background.
logo-dont-effects: Add shadows, outlines or other effects.
logo-dont-retype: Retype the name in another font, or rearrange the parts.
logo-license-cc: Like the rest of this project’s images, the logo files are shared under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license (CC BY 4.0). You can use and adapt them for any purpose, including commercially, as long as you credit BetterMati.org and link to the license.
logo-license-requests: The do’s and don’ts above are requests to keep the logo recognizable, not extra license terms.
logo-license-endorse: BetterMati is an independent civic project, not the City Government of Mati. The license doesn’t let you suggest that BetterMati endorses you or your use. Please also don’t put the logo on anything that could pass for an official City document or announcement.
logo-license-others: The Feel Mati and BetterGov.ph logos that also appear on this site aren’t BetterMati’s, and this page doesn’t cover them.

trans-description: City of Mati’s FY2025 reported finances, 2026–2027 planning figures and selected procurement records, with official sources.
trans-units: Amounts in millions of Philippine pesos (M)
trans-finance-note: FY2025 reported figures are from DBM BESF 2027, Table F.13. External receipts include NTA; non-income receipts include borrowing. SEF is the Special Education Fund. Non-operating expenditures include capital outlay and principal debt payments. These financial flows are not the approved annual budget.
trans-cash-note: Ending cash is shown after prior-year payable payments and continuing appropriations. It is not simply receipts minus expenditures. Amounts retain the source’s rounding to two decimal places.
trans-project-unknowns: Contractor, award amount and physical completion have not been verified from this notice. A procurement status does not prove delivery or completion.
trans-project-11374254: Level II potable water supply system in Barangay Badas
trans-project-11439666: Completion works for the cultural and sports center in Dahican
trans-audit-note: This compilation does not assess audit compliance. The COA report directory is provided for further research; a Mati audit report was not retrieved during this check.
stats-verified-intro: Population, city finances, and poverty estimates for Mati, with source links and reference years.
stats-checked-on: Sources checked: {{date}}. Each figure uses the latest reference period verified for that indicator.
stats-finance-period: FY2025 actual receipts, published in DBM BESF 2027 on 11 August 2026. Based on local treasurers’ LIFT submissions to DOF-BLGF.
stats-receipts-note: Total receipts include non-income receipts such as borrowings. NTA is already included in external sources. These are reported receipts, not the approved budget or a COA audit opinion.
stats-poverty-definition: Estimated share of Mati’s population with income below the poverty threshold. PSA small area estimates, with 90% confidence intervals.
stats-poverty-release: Reference years: 2018, 2021 and 2023. Released 6 February 2026. Values were checked in an archived copy of PSA’s workbook (Mati, PSGC 112509); the direct PSA download was unavailable during this review.
stats-economic-unverified: City-level business counts, agricultural land, employment rates and sector shares have not been verified in a dated official source. Previously displayed figures are withheld. Provincial or regional rates are not substituted for Mati data.
stats-cmci-unverified: Mati’s recent CMCI scores and rankings could not be verified because the DTI profile was inaccessible. Previously displayed scores, trends and indicator bars are withheld pending verification. Rankings must identify their city category.
trans-outlook-note: These amounts are published in DBM’s BESF 2027. We classify them as planning figures because the publication predates the end of 2026 and all of 2027. The tables reuse actual-data footnotes without separately explaining estimates. They are not verified full-year actuals or evidence of an enacted city budget. Amounts are in PHP millions; NTA is included in receipts.
trans-project-1713: Rice assistance for indigent individuals or families
leg-records-scope: Selected references, not a complete register. No 2025–2026 records have been verified for this collection. This does not mean no measures were passed.
leg-records-evidence: Government reporting identifies the numbers and subjects below. Summaries are not official titles. Signed texts, session dates, amendments and current legal status remain unverified.
leg-record-abunda: Establishment of the Abunda Festival to recognize farmers, fisherfolk and livestock raisers.
leg-record-meat: Ordinance cited by the city veterinarian in enforcement against undocumented processed meat products. The report does not supply its official title.
leg-record-eagle: Establishment of a 7,000-hectare Philippine Eagle Sanctuary, as reported by PNA. Issued by Mati’s former municipal council.
leg-legal-source: Legal basis: Republic Act No. 9408, sections 17–21
leg-budget-rule: Appropriations require an ordinance or law; a resolution alone does not replace an appropriations ordinance.
leg-copy-heading: How to verify the full record
leg-copy-body: Request a certified copy from the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Mati. Include the measure’s number and year; ask for the signed text, passage date, amendments and posting or publication record. Fees prescribed by ordinance may apply.
leg-copy-source: RA 9408: duties of the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlungsod
leg-archive-unavailable: The previously linked Mati council archive could not be retrieved during this review (24 September 2026).
rising-preview-note: Projects with published sources. Statuses reflect the dated records, not live construction updates.
rising-note: Selected projects in Mati with source links and dated evidence. Bidding ceilings, appropriations, announced funding and reported costs mean different things; these amounts are not added to the city’s annual spending. This is not a complete inventory.
rising-airport-detail: The 2026 national budget lists ₱700 million for Mati Airport under DOTr. This is an appropriation, not a contract award or actual expenditure, and this budget document does not establish construction progress or an opening date. The 2027 budget proposal has no separate line for Mati Airport.
rising-macambol-detail: PNA reports Hallmark Mining Corp.’s statement that the Silad–Banluton water system was completed and serves about 250 households. Funded through the company’s Social Development and Management Program (SDMP); not city expenditure. No independent completion certificate was reviewed.
rising-fishport-detail: A February 2023 PNA report quotes the city’s announcement of ₱150 million in additional funding for Phase 2. The announcement does not establish the contract price, actual spending or present completion.
rising-coastal: Fish port access road and coastal highway
rising-coastal-detail: The city announced ₱2 billion for a 2.25-kilometre route linking Mati Park and Baywalk, the fish port and Sitio Bilawan in February 2023, with DPWH coordination. Current construction progress is unverified. This does not confirm the former “Baywalk & Boulevard Extension” listing.
rising-matiao-road-detail: The President's proposed 2027 national budget lists ₱100 million for the Matiao–Magsaysay Coastal Road in Barangay Matiao, City of Mati, under DPWH (Region XI). This is a proposal: Congress may change or remove it, and it is not an appropriation, a contract or actual spending.
rising-procurement-detail: The PhilGEPS notice is marked Awarded. Its ABC is a bidding ceiling, not the awarded amount. Physical completion and current operation have not been verified.

a11y-page-lede: BetterMati.org aims to make public information about the City of Mati usable by as many people as possible, including people who use screen readers, navigate by keyboard, or browse on a phone over a slow connection.
a11y-page-standard-body: We use WCAG 2.1 Level AA as our working accessibility goal. This statement is not a formal certification or the result of a third-party audit.
a11y-page-approach-standard: WCAG 2.1 Level AA is the goal we design and review against. Changes are checked with automated audits (Lighthouse) and by hand with a keyboard and at phone widths before they ship.
a11y-page-approach-means: No independent accessibility audit has been done yet, so some pages may not meet every success criterion. When we find a gap, we treat it as a bug to fix, not a known exception.
a11y-page-measure-semantic-desc: Pages use header, navigation, main and footer landmarks, and headings follow the visible order of the content, so screen-reader users can move around by structure.
a11y-page-measure-keyboard-desc: Links, buttons, menus and search fields can be reached and used with a keyboard, and every focusable element shows a visible focus outline.
a11y-page-measure-alt-desc: Meaningful images carry descriptive alternative text. Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology so they are not read aloud.
a11y-page-measure-contrast-desc: Body text, links and secondary text use colours chosen to meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background.
a11y-page-measure-motion-desc: If your device is set to reduce motion, sliding and scaling animations are switched off and content simply fades in.
a11y-page-measure-languages-desc: The site can be switched between English and Cebuano, and the page language changes with it so screen readers use the right pronunciation.
a11y-page-limit-pdf-desc: Some linked documents, such as the City's Citizen's Charter, are PDFs published by the City Government and may not be tagged for screen readers.
a11y-page-limit-external-desc: Links to official government portals and other external services lead to sites we do not control, which may not behave the same way as this one.
a11y-page-limit-translations-desc: The Cebuano translation is still a small starter set, so many pages fall back to English until a full translation is reviewed.
a11y-page-limits-note: If part of the site is hard to use with assistive technology, telling us which page and what happened helps us find where to improve.
a11y-page-feedback-text: Tell us what you were trying to do, which page the problem happened on, and the browser or assistive technology you were using.

finance-lede: What the City of Mati received and spent each year from FY{{from}} to FY{{to}}, as reported to the national government, with the 2026–2027 outlook.
finance-note: Figures are the City Treasurer’s own reports: yearly totals compiled by the Bureau of Local Government Finance and published by DBM, and the 2026 quarterly report and special funds as posted by BLGF and the City. None is a COA-audited statement.
finance-trend-lede: Each year comes from a different DBM edition. Compare the totals, but don't add years together or treat one year's ending cash as the next year's opening cash.
finance-allotment-note: FY2021 reports the Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA); from FY2022 it became the National Tax Allotment (NTA). The allotment is already counted in external receipts.
finance-catalog-lede: Every amount on this page comes from one of these official reports. DBM table links open at Mati’s page; BLGF workbooks and City postings download as spreadsheets.
finance-crosscheck-note: The Bureau of Local Government Finance publishes the same FY2025 report as a workbook; every amount matches once rounded.
finance-ytd-lede: What the City collected and spent in the first nine months of 2026, set against its own 2026 income targets and appropriations.
finance-ytd-progress-title: Collected and spent so far, against the 2026 budget
finance-ytd-progress-help: Nine of twelve months have passed (75%). A bar well below that is not necessarily a problem: some income arrives late in the year, and projects are often paid on completion.
finance-ytd-note: Figures are the City Treasurer’s preliminary quarterly report, cumulative from 1 January, as compiled by the Bureau of Local Government Finance. The budget amounts are the targets and appropriations printed on the City’s own copy of the same report, posted under the Full Disclosure Policy. Neither is audited.
finance-funds-title: The 20% Development Fund and the disaster fund
finance-funds-lede: Two funds the law sets aside from the City’s budget, and how much of each has been used, from the City’s own reports.
finance-funds-df-desc: At least 20% of the National Tax Allotment must go to development projects. Committed means a contract or obligation has been made; it is not yet money paid out.
finance-funds-df-projects: Programs and projects with nothing committed yet
finance-funds-df-note: From the City’s third-quarter report, signed by the City Budget Officer and the Mayor. Its project table adds up to ₱127.11M because one subtotal (₱9.87M) is also entered on a line that says no obligation was incurred; the form’s own summary, ₱117.24M, is shown here.
finance-funds-drr-desc: At least 5% of regular income is set aside for disasters: 70% for preparedness and mitigation, and 30% as a Quick Response Fund for relief and recovery.
finance-funds-drr-note: Preliminary figures compiled by the Bureau of Local Government Finance. They show how much was spent, not on what; the City’s quarterly disaster fund reports on the Full Disclosure page give the detail.
finance-read-source-desc: Each figure is the city treasurer's own submission through the LIFT system, compiled by the Bureau of Local Government Finance and published by DBM. It is not a COA audit.
finance-read-editions-desc: Each year comes from a different DBM edition. Ending and opening cash don't always match between editions (FY2021 to FY2022, and FY2024 to FY2025); both are shown as published.
finance-read-borrowing-desc: Non-income receipts are mostly loans taken out that year. They add to total receipts but are not revenue.
projects-lede: Major projects in Mati and the City’s procurement notices, searchable and each linked to its official source. Amounts are budget ceilings or appropriations, not money spent.
projects-notices-lede: The City of Mati’s notices listed on PhilGEPS when we checked, plus earlier records with a known outcome. This is not a complete procurement history. National and city procurements are labelled separately and are not added to the city’s annual figures.
projects-search-projects: Search by project, place, status or source…
projects-search-notices: Search by notice, solicitation number, PhilGEPS reference or category…
projects-no-match: Nothing matches these filters. Try another search or clear the filters.
projects-sale-note: Sale of City property: the amount is the minimum bid, not a purchase budget.
projects-open-notice: Open the official notice for {{title}} (opens in a new tab)
projects-notices-footnote: Status is as shown on the official notice on the date checked; it is not updated automatically. ABC is the Approved Budget for the Contract: the bidding ceiling, not the contract price or money spent.
fdp-lede: Under the DILG's Full Disclosure Policy, every city must publish 14 kinds of financial reports. This page lists the ones found for Mati: the City's postings on the DILG portal, and archived copies of older reports from its old website.
fdp-about-title: From the DILG portal and the Internet Archive
fdp-about-body: Reports from {{portalFrom}} on are the City's own postings on the DILG Full Disclosure portal. Reports from {{archiveFrom}}–{{archiveTo}} are Internet Archive copies of files from the City's old website. Years in between are missing.
fdp-portal-link: Open the DILG Full Disclosure portal
fdp-types-lede: Each report answers a plain question about the City's money. The count shows how many are listed here.
fdp-search: Search report type, title or period
fdp-from-portal: Listed on the DILG portal; link checked {{date}}
fdp-unavailable: The portal returns an error for this file
fdp-read-title: What these records are, and are not
fdp-read-verification-desc: Archived files were opened one by one, and their titles and periods are as printed. Portal postings are listed as the portal shows them, and each download link was tried; a file the portal can't serve is marked.
fdp-read-coverage-desc: The portal listing covers what the City posted from 2024 on, and the archive only reports from 2012–2014. Years in between, and any report the City did not post, are missing. A missing report doesn't mean the City never published it.
fdp-read-archive-desc: Portal links download the City's spreadsheet from the DILG portal. Archived links open the Internet Archive's copy of an old City file. For anything missing, ask the City Budget Office.
docs-lede: The City's charter, ordinances and application forms that could be found and opened, with a note on how current each one is.
docs-about-body: Most City documents are no longer on mati.gov.ph. This library lists what could be opened, and marks archived copies and documents that no longer open.
docs-search: Search title, type, office or year
docs-read-title: Check the date before you rely on it
docs-read-verification-desc: Every document was opened before it was listed, and its title and edition are taken from the document itself.
docs-read-currency-desc: Archived copies show what the City once posted. Rates, forms and requirements may have changed since; confirm with the office named.
docs-read-coverage-desc: This is not the City's full document register. Ordinances and resolutions are on the Legislation pages; finance reports are on City finances.
method-lede: The rules every page on BetterMati.org follows, how a record gets from an official source onto the site, and what that record can and cannot prove.
method-rule-source-desc: Each number, name or requirement points to the office or document that stands behind it, with a link wherever one exists.
method-rule-missing-desc: When a value isn't in the source, it is left blank or marked unknown. It is never filled with zero or an estimate.
method-rule-periods: Publication year is not reporting year
method-rule-periods-desc: A 2027 report about 2025 is labelled 2025. Planning figures are kept apart from reported results.
method-rule-combine-desc: Figures from different reports or editions are shown side by side, not added together or bridged when they don't match.
method-rule-ceilings-desc: A bid ceiling (ABC) or an appropriation is shown as what it is, never as money paid or a project finished.
method-rule-checked: Every record shows when it was checked
method-rule-checked-desc: Pages and datasets carry the date they were last checked against the source, so you can judge how fresh they are.
method-process-title: From an official source to the site
method-step-find-desc: Locate the official source: a government report, portal, notice or the City’s own document.
method-step-verify-desc: Open it and read the record directly. Scanned tables are rendered and read column by column, and totals are re-added.
method-step-record-desc: Write the values into the data files with the source, page, period and check date. Research notes record what could not be confirmed.
method-step-publish-desc: The site is rebuilt from those files. Tests fail if a figure loses its source or a draft is shown as verified.
method-evidence-title: What a record can and cannot establish
method-can-1: That an official source published a figure, notice or document, and when.
method-can-2: What the source says, exactly as printed.
method-can-3: How figures in the same source relate, such as receipts against expenditures.
method-cannot-title: On its own, it does not prove
method-cannot-1: That money was actually paid, or a project completed.
method-cannot-2: That the figure was audited or is free of errors.
method-cannot-3: That nothing else exists beyond what was found.
method-privacy-title: What is published, and what is held back
method-privacy-published-desc: Public records about the City's government: officials' names and positions, finances, notices, laws and forms.
method-privacy-withheld-desc: Personal contact details that the City hasn't confirmed for public use, and anything about private residents. Visitor data is covered by the Privacy Policy.
method-corrections-text: Report a wrong figure or a broken link with the "Report a data issue" button at the bottom of any page. Fixes are recorded in the changelog, and each dataset's check date is updated when it is re-checked.
transparency-lede: The City of Mati's finances, projects, Full Disclosure reports and official documents, each traced to the source it came from.
transparency-note: BetterMati.org is volunteer-run and not the official City Government website.
transparency-find-finance: What the City received and spent each year, from DBM's published tables.
transparency-find-projects: Major projects and the City’s procurement notices, searchable.
transparency-find-fdp: Budget, fund and procurement reports the City is required to publish.
transparency-find-docs: The City's charter, ordinances and application forms.
transparency-find-legislation: Ordinances and resolutions of the Sangguniang Panlungsod.
transparency-find-statistics: Population, poverty and barangay figures from the PSA.
transparency-find-method: The rules the site follows and the limits of what records prove.
transparency-data-eyebrow: Know where the data comes from
transparency-gaps-lede: These gaps are listed so nobody mistakes a missing record for a record that does not exist.
transparency-gap-fdp-desc: Reports after 2014 are on the DILG portal but not yet indexed here; its city filter could not be read automatically.
transparency-gap-audit-desc: Annual audit reports for the City are published by COA, but its website blocks automated access. None are summarised here.
transparency-read-title: Three things to keep in mind
transparency-read-complete-desc: Each page shows what could be found and checked. Gaps are named rather than filled.
transparency-read-interchangeable-desc: A budget, a bid ceiling and an expenditure measure different things. They are never added together.
transparency-read-archived-desc: Older City documents come from archived copies. Check the date, and confirm with the City before relying on them.
search-lede: Search every page, service, City office, project, procurement notice, document and official link on the site.
search-placeholder: Search for a service, office, project or document…
search-empty: Nothing on the site matches that search. Try other words, or browse the
search-fdp-desc: Full Disclosure report · City of Mati postings on the DILG portal
map-lede: How published project records are spread across Mati's 26 barangays.
map-hint: Point at or select a barangay to see its project records.
map-hint-compact: Point at a barangay to see how many project records name it.
map-svg-label: Map of the 26 barangays of Mati, turned on its side with north to the left, shaded by number of project records
map-attribution: Barangay boundaries: faeldon/philippines-json-maps (from altcoder/philippines-psgc-shapefiles, PSGC 2023). Barangay codes and names: Philippine Statistics Authority PSGC, CC BY 4.0. Boundaries are approximate and coastal barangays extend into municipal waters.
map-records_one: {{count}} published project record names this barangay.
map-records_other: {{count}} published project records name this barangay.
map-none: No published project record names this barangay yet. That does not mean nothing was built here: many City records give no barangay, and four quarters of bid results could not be downloaded.
map-citywide-note_one: {{count}} citywide or unassigned record is not listed under any barangay.
map-citywide-note_other: {{count}} citywide or unassigned records are not listed under any barangay.
map-equation: {{attributed}} attributed across {{barangays}} barangays + {{citywide}} citywide / unassigned = {{total}} published project records. A record naming two barangays counts in both shadings but once in the total.
map-density-help: Shading shows how many published project records name each barangay.
map-read-1: A record counts for a barangay only when its own source names it: the Location column of the City's Bid Results on Civil Works, a PhilGEPS or DPWH notice, or the report behind a major project. Goods and services purchases are not mapped.
map-read-2: Shading counts records, not money, and does not mark an exact site, parcel or road segment. Records come from the bid results the City posted for Q4 2023 to Q2 2026 (four quarters could not be downloaded), current notices and major projects.
works-title: Construction the City has bid out
works-lede: Civil works the City's Bids and Awards Committee reported as awarded, from its own quarterly Full Disclosure reports: where each is, its budget ceiling, the winning contractor and bid. These records shade the project map above.
works-stat-bids-caption: {{count}} works, against {{abc}} in budget ceilings; not final costs or spending
works-open-report: Open the City’s Bid Results report for {{period}} ({{title}})
works-footnote: Transcribed row by row from the City's “Bid Results on Civil Works” reports (FDP Form 10a) on the DILG Full Disclosure portal. The winning bid is what the contractor offered, not the final contract cost or what was actually spent, and these reports don't say whether the work was finished. Reports for Q2 2024 and Q2–Q4 2025 could not be downloaded from the portal, so their works are missing. One Q1 2026 bid is shown exactly as the City printed it because it can't be read as a number.
volunteer-dialog-desc: BetterMati.org is a volunteer-built civic project. Designers, developers, writers, and translators are all welcome.
service-search-default-placeholder: Search services (e.g., birth certificate, business permit)
attraction-draft-note: Some details on this page haven’t been confirmed by the City Tourism Office yet. Check them before you travel.
visit-photos-lede: Who published each photo of a place on this page, and where. Places without a sourced photo show a placeholder until one is found.
visit-photos-terms: Photos from the City Government of Mati, its City Tourism Office and the Philippine Carabao Center were published on those offices’ own websites and are credited to them. Philippine law gives works of the government no copyright (Republic Act 8293, Section 176), though using them for profit needs the agency’s approval; BetterMati is non-profit. City photos are cited through Internet Archive copies because the City’s website currently loads unrelated outside content. Photos from Wikimedia Commons are used under the Creative Commons license shown. If you took one of these photos and want it credited differently or removed, email volunteer@bettermati.org.
